scope: Focused predictive nomination wargame. Fresh AP election-survey and official oversight-source checks; candidate detail and administration assessments carried from existing research. No full daily intake, new post-election primary poll or complete donor/organization audit.

methodology_change.basis: Predictive reasoning about voter attribution, candidate reactions and oversight is authorized under this dated methodology revision; roster changes require separate authorization.

summary: Vance retains the strongest starting route but loses some advantage once persistent costs, senior responsibility and a credible alternative are explicitly weighed. DeSantis becomes the leading approved alternative. Neither a disloyalty trap nor a successful Trump-authorized reset is inevitable.

sources_checked.description: Original AP account of its voter survey, fielded October 19/22–November 3. Policy responsibility, costs, corruption, candidate quality and demand for checks; election electorate, not a 2028 primary poll.
Official investigation and document-preservation demands ahead of incoming committee chairmanship; allegations and intended process, not adjudicated findings.

changes: Replaced inherited weights with an explicit five-branch subjective mixture.
Adjudicated six strategic questions and opposing cases for every candidate; attached observable tests.
Updated current nomination summaries from the same evidence, retaining factual faction access and policy findings. Candidate probabilities are not independent evidence of faction power.
cross_report_implications: Existing Vance fundraising/access supports continuity capacity; war advocacy and post-election differentiation create competing responsibility and correction paths. No faction endorsement is inferred.
Hegseth pressure and Wiles/Miller transition identify mechanisms for attempted selective blame, not a proven reset or completed removal.
Oversight pressure can constrain officeholders, but a candidate forecast does not change an exercised-authority score.
DeSantis/McEntee coalition transfer remains a projection, not a new faction alignment.
gaps: Scenario weights and conditional shares are subjective and uncalibrated; arithmetic does not validate the inputs.
No post-election primary candidate poll, full FEC audit, new entry commitment or early-state organizational audit was verified. Existing historical evidence remains dated.
Freshly read AP election survey and official preservation demands inform the environment. Candidate policy and conduct records are carried from the prior pass, not wholly reverified.
Search results suggested newer Vance diplomacy and Democratic priorities stories, but full pages failed to load; they were not used as verified updates.
The election survey describes the midterm electorate, not the next primary electorate or a causal decomposition of vote choice.
Unlisted-field risk is material and unquantified; no nominees were added.
validation: Reproducible mixture, scenario totals, exact roster, evidence references, append-only history, candidate opposition and dated-test checks required before publication.
